slides.title: What is C#?
slides.content: C# (pronounced 'C Sharp') is a modern, object-oriented programming language developed by Microsoft. It is designed to be simple, efficient, and type-safe.

slides.title: History and Versions
slides.content: C# was first released in 2002 as version 1.0. It has evolved through many versions, now at C# 12, with regular updates adding new features.

slides.title: What Can C# Do?
slides.content: C# is used for web and mobile apps, desktop software, video games with Unity, and cloud services. It is a versatile language for many platforms.

slides.title: .NET Ecosystem
slides.content: .NET Framework runs only on Windows, while .NET (formerly .NET Core) is cross-platform and open-source. .NET 5 and later unify these into a single platform.

slides.title: The CLR and JIT Compiler
slides.content: The Common Language Runtime (CLR) manages code execution, and the JIT compiler converts bytecode to native machine code at runtime. Together, they provide memory management and security.

slides.title: Your First C# Program
slides.content: A C# program starts with a class containing a Main method, which is the entry point where execution begins.

slides.title: Namespaces and using Directives
slides.content: Namespaces organize code into logical groups, and the 'using' directive brings those names into your file so you can use them directly.

slides.title: Classes and the Main Method
slides.content: A class defines the structure and behavior of objects, and Main is the static method where the program starts running.

slides.title: Flow Builder: Hello World
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to drag an Output block and print 'Hello, World!'. This is your first step in thinking about code as a flow of instructions.
